Refund tax should use `decimal.ROUND_DOWN`. Invoice tax stays on `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so the two need separate rounding modes. I'm going on your word about what finance said, since nothing in the repo records it.

- **Memory:** the project had a stored decision that all tax uses `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (March 2026). I changed it to cover invoice tax only. I also added a new decision for refund tax, with `src/billing/tax.py` as the file that would invalidate it.
- **Code:** I found no rounding code in the repo (no `ROUND_*` or `quantize` calls). I haven't changed any code, so the refund path in `src/billing/tax.py` still needs to be written or updated.

If you want, I can implement it now. Make sure refunds don't reuse an invoice rounding helper that has `HALF_EVEN` fixed in.

I'd have wanted an `update` parameter like `append_note` or `amend_reason` that keeps the prior text in history. A `related_to` or `refines` link from the new memory to the old one would also have helped, and I settled for mentioning each in the other's text.

2. **Recording where a claim came from.** The refund rule rests on the user's report of what finance said that morning. `create` has no `source` or `reference` field for who said it or a ticket link, so I put the date in the free-text content. A `source` parameter would let later sessions judge how much to trust it.

3. **Checking the memory's scope against the code.** Both memories point to `src/billing/tax.py`, but my grep found no rounding code in the repo, so I couldn't confirm the file exists. `create` and `update` accept any path without checking it. A `physical` path validation warning would have flagged this.

I never loaded the deferred tools (`verify`, `resolve`, `task_current`), so I can't say whether they would have covered items 1 and 3. I used `get`, `update` and `create` without trouble.
